body:
## Why

`hkb groom` and `/kanban:groom` (siblings) are not shipped until the packaging knows about them. hkb installs
commands by reading the `commands/` directory rather than a list, so the command needs no code change to be
installed — but several **fixed lists** are spelled out deliberately, in tests and in the smoke script, and they
are what actually prove the tarball ships the file.

## What

Per #191's *Registration and docs* section.

- **Tests that enumerate**: `test/init.test.js`'s file list and its `commandNames()` assertion gain `groom`;
  `test/skill.test.js`'s doctor string becomes `/kanban:decompose, /kanban:groom, /kanban:operate,
  /kanban:specify not registered — the skill documents them`.
- **`scripts/smoke-pack.mjs`**: `commands/groom.md` in `MUST_SHIP`, `.claude/commands/kanban/groom.md` in
  `FROM_PACKAGE` — so `npm run smoke` proves the packed tarball installs it.
- **Docs**: the README planning table gains a third row and `hkb groom` joins the snippet beside
  `hkb dispatch --dry-run`; `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s description names four commands; `src/cli.js`'s HELP
  gains the verb; one sentence in `skills/kanban/references/protocol.md` under the tick saying `hkb groom` is a
  read like `dispatch --dry-run` — no status, label or transition changes.
- **The wiki**: a new page `docs/wiki/features/backlog-grooming.md` from `docs/wiki/_templates/page.md`;
  `planning-commands.md` re-stamped; `index.md` and `log.md` updated. Re-stamp only the `covers` shas for files
  this track actually changed — leave unrelated drift visible rather than silently stamping it.

## Done when

- [ ] `test/init.test.js` and the doctor "not registered" string list four commands.
- [ ] `npm run smoke` packs, installs and finds `groom.md` in both places.
- [ ] README, plugin.json, HELP and the protocol.md sentence are in place.
- [ ] `docs/wiki/features/backlog-grooming.md` exists and `node .repolore/scripts/wiki-check.mjs` reports no
      staleness **caused by this track**.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test && npm run smoke` pass. `src/model.js` and `skills/kanban/SKILL.md` are not
      touched by this task.

## Contract

These are the names, signatures and rules a sibling depends on. Do not invent alternatives; a change here
breaks a task you cannot see.

- **The eleven "Amendments from the adversarial pass" at the top of #191 override its body wherever they
  differ.** Read `hkb show 191` first and treat the amendments as the specification. In particular: reuse
  `computeReady`, `agentsOf` and the walk in `src/track.js` — **do not write `detectCycles`**; `no_goal` is
  `info` when the body already has a Done-when heading; `broad_path` exists and is `ask`; `overlap_pair.why` is
  guard-aware.
- `groomBoard(tasks, { now, caps, pairs = 10, statuses })` is exported from `src/model.js` and takes the raw
  `fetchBoard` array and nothing else — a later card puts the same function behind `hkb serve`'s snapshot.
- `GROOM_KINDS` and `GROOM_ACTIONS` are exported from `src/model.js`. Actions are the closed vocabulary
  `promote · specify · link-under · split · supersede · reprioritise · park · archive`, plus `judge` and `none`.
- `fetchBoard(ctx, { blockers: 'all' })` REST-fills blockers for **every open card** on a repo without GraphQL
  `blockedBy`; `blockers: true` keeps today's todo/blocked-only behaviour.
- The `--json` field names in #191 are **frozen**; later kinds are added to `findings`, never renamed.
- The CLI never emits the word "duplicate". `overlap_pair.why` is "will serialize under path_overlap".
- **`src/dispatch.js` is untouched by this whole track** — the promote step still filters `status === 'todo'`.
- Nothing in this track writes to the board. `hkb groom` is a read, like `hkb dispatch --dry-run`.
goal: The enumerated lists in test/init.test.js and the doctor string name four commands, npm run smoke finds groom.md in the tarball and the install, README/plugin.json/HELP/protocol.md name the verb, and docs/wiki/features/backlog-grooming.md exists with no staleness caused by this track
title: Ship groom: registration lists, smoke-pack, README, plugin.json, HELP and the wiki page
